en: May that Goddess who is the supreme sovereign of all beings, who is established in the gods, and who exists in the form of Caṇḍikā, dispel my sin. (1)
Salutation to the Goddess, the Great Goddess; salutation ever to Śivā.
Salutation to Prakṛti, to Bhadrā; we, being self-restrained, bow down before her.
Constant salutations to Durgā, to her who carries one across difficulties, to Sārā, to the accomplisher of all things, to Khyāti, as well as to Kṛṣṇā and Dhūmrā. || 3 ||
Salutations again and again to her who is exceedingly gentle and exceedingly fierce;
salutations again and again to the Goddess Kṛtyā, the foundation of the universe. || 4 ||
To that Goddess who, among all beings, is designated by the name Viṣṇumātrā—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 5 ||
To that Goddess who is designated as consciousness within all beings—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! (6)
To that Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of the supreme speech—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 7 ||
To that Goddess who dwells within all beings in the form of sleep—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! (8)
To that Goddess who dwells within all beings in the form of hunger—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 9 ||
Salutations to that Goddess who dwells within all beings in the form of craving; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again. || 10 ||
To that Goddess who dwells in all beings in the form of patience—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 11 ||
To that Goddess who is established in all beings in the form of birth—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 12 ||
To that Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of peace—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 13 ||
To that Goddess who dwells within all beings in the form of the memory of the Lord—salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again. || 14 ||
To that Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of compassion—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 15 ||
Salutations to that Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of contentment; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.
Salutations to that Goddess who resides in all beings in the form of satisfaction; salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again. || 17 ||
To that Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of the practice of austerity—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 18 ||
To that Goddess who is established in all beings in the form of a mother—homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage again and again! || 19 ||
Speech and the other [senses] are not its object; the Great Tripurā is the cause of all.
That which is her supreme form abides as the innermost of all. (20)
The best of yogis perceive it in the external region, and no others;
its other form, which is gross, is within the range of everyone.

She is of massive form, possessing eighteen arms, most beautiful, seated upon a lion; free from worldly desire, she grants the state sought by petitioners, golden-hued and ever-increasing in splendor.
Unsurpassed, faultless, infinite, and of wondrous form; her conduct transcends the world, she is the full moon who bestows supreme purity. (23)
You are the primordial one whose body comprises all that is moving and unmoving; you are the multitude of worlds and the refuge for those who take shelter in you.
Indeed, having taken recourse to your own sovereign power, you shine forth, for there is no other refuge whatsoever for you.
O Goddess, remover of the distress of those who have sought refuge, be gracious; be gracious, O Mother of the entire world!
Be gracious, O Sovereign of the Universe; protect the universe, for you, O Goddess, are the Mistress of all that is moving and unmoving. 25.
